problem: Computational lithography requires optimizing mask designs through a multi-stage continuous physical process (mask optimization, optical imaging, resist exposure, development), but existing models fail to capture the complete pipeline dynamics.
approach: LithoDreamer formulates the lithography pipeline as a multi-step evolution system with physics-informed latent spaces, using contrastive variational optimization to guide process interventions without continuous supervision.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in forward evolution and inverse planning for computational lithography by capturing feature changes between adjacent stages.

problem: Video diffusion models struggle to maintain geometric consistency when given precise camera pose controls, as directly injecting camera parameters often causes structural distortions.
approach: CameraNoise encodes camera motion into the noise space via geometry-guided reprojection flow, decoupling motion from scene appearance while preserving the Gaussian prior of diffusion.
contribution: Delivers stable, high-fidelity videos with faithful camera trajectory control by embedding poses directly into noise rather than conditioning on parameters.

problem: Learning dexterous manipulation from human demonstrations requires handling large action spaces, spatiotemporal discontinuities, and bridging the embodiment gap between human and robot hands in long-horizon bimanual tasks.
approach: DexMachina uses curriculum learning with virtual object controllers of decaying strength, allowing policies to gradually take over as the object is driven toward target states under motion and contact guidance.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines on bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks and provides a functional comparison benchmark for evaluating hardware designs.

problem: Causal discovery from observational data is expensive, requiring many domain expert queries to reliably identify causal edges and directions in directed acyclic graphs.
approach: A Bayesian framework that actively queries experts about edge relations using expected information gain, with a flexible particle approximation modeling noisy expert judgments over edge existence and direction.
contribution: Achieves faster posterior concentration and improved recovery of directed causal effects under tight query budgets on synthetic and biological datasets.

problem: Automatic speech recognition systems remain vulnerable to adversarial audio examples in physical settings, where prior perturbation-minimizing approaches fail to achieve sufficient stealthiness against real ASR systems.
approach: Introduces music carrier selection and an attention-aware stealthiness loss to generate adversarial perturbations that sound benign, achieving high attack success while preserving audio naturalness.
contribution: In user studies with 200 participants, 55.6% perceived the adversarial examples as benign audio, a 20% improvement over prior methods on both commercial APIs and voice assistants.

problem: Developing proactive agents that monitor environments and take initiative is hindered by the lack of specialized datasets and task structure understanding for domains like assistance, maintenance, and safety monitoring.
approach: ProAct-75 benchmark with 91,581 annotations and explicit task graphs encoding step dependencies, paired with ProAct-Helper, an MLLM baseline that uses state detection and entropy-driven heuristic search for action selection.
contribution: ProAct-Helper improves trigger detection mF1 by 6.21%, reduces steps by 0.25, and increases parallel action rate by 15.58% compared to strong closed-source baselines.

problem: Long-horizon LLM-based agents struggle with credit assignment because sparse outcome-based rewards make it hard to identify which intermediate steps drove success.
approach: Entropy-Modulated Policy Gradients (EMPG) recalibrates learning signals based on step-wise uncertainty and task outcomes, amplifying updates for confident correct actions while attenuating uncertain steps.
contribution: Achieves substantial performance gains on WebShop, ALFWorld, and Deep Search benchmarks, significantly outperforming policy gradient baselines through uncertainty-aware credit assignment.

problem: LLM ensembling improves performance but incurs high computational cost because it requires separate forward passes through each model to explicitly compute the full ensemble distribution.
approach: Mixture-model-like Ensemble (ME) reinterprets ensembling as a mixture model, stochastically selecting a single model per token generation step rather than computing all outputs.
contribution: Achieves 1.78x-2.68x faster inference than conventional ensembling while maintaining equivalent performance, mathematically equivalent to sampling from ensemble distribution.

problem: LLM agents waste resources by retaining all thoughts and observations across multi-turn interactions, even though their necessity and utility varies across turns and impacts both efficiency and effectiveness.
approach: Agent-Omit learns to adaptively omit redundant thoughts and observations through fine-tuning on synthesis data and omit-aware reinforcement learning with dual sampling and tailored rewards.
contribution: Agent-Omit-8B achieves performance comparable to frontier models while obtaining the best effectiveness-efficiency trade-off, with theoretical KL-divergence bound on omission policy deviation.

problem: LLM inference and training are computationally expensive despite most parameters and FLOPs being in the feedforward layers, which can be sparsified without harming performance.
approach: Introduces a sparse packing format and CUDA kernels for efficient sparse computation, paired with L1 regularization during training to induce unstructured sparsity in feedforward layers.
contribution: Achieves over 99% sparsity with negligible performance loss, translating to substantial throughput, energy efficiency, and memory benefits that scale with model size.

problem: Traditional GraphRAG methods suffer from high construction costs, fixed one-time retrieval, and reliance on long-context reasoning, limiting their practical deployment for knowledge-grounded generation.
approach: Graph-R1 models retrieval as multi-turn agent-environment interaction with lightweight hypergraph construction, optimizing the agent via end-to-end reinforcement learning.
contribution: Outperforms traditional GraphRAG and RL-enhanced RAG methods in reasoning accuracy, retrieval efficiency, and generation quality on standard RAG benchmarks.

problem: Reinforcement learning for LLM reasoning is prohibitively resource-intensive, requiring extensive reward signals and substantial rollout costs during training.
approach: Dynamic One-Shot Policy Refinement (DoPR) uses uncertainty-aware selection to choose a single informative training sample per batch, guided by reward volatility and exploration-driven acquisition.
contribution: Reduces rollout overhead by nearly an order of magnitude while maintaining competitive reasoning accuracy on reasoning-intensive LLM applications.

problem: Text-guided object segmentation requires both cross-modal reasoning and precise pixel grounding, but single forward passes limit verification and refinement when initial localization is incorrect.
approach: RSAgent is an agentic MLLM that interleaves reasoning and action through multi-turn tool invocations, revising pixel hypotheses iteratively based on visual feedback.
contribution: Achieves 66.5% gIoU on ReasonSeg zero-shot (9% improvement) and 81.5% cIoU on RefCOCOg, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on both in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks.

problem: Large audio language models struggle to maintain consistent speaking style across multi-turn role-play dialogues because there is no objective metric for quantifying and rewarding stylistic consistency.
approach: Mean Continuation Log-Probability (MCLP) measures the likelihood of ground-truth speech tokens conditioned on context history, serving as an evaluation metric and reinforcement learning reward.
contribution: MCLP aligns well with human judgments of stylistic consistency and effectively improves style alignment between generated speech and role-play instructions.

problem: Spatiotemporal field reconstruction from sparse sensor observations is challenging when target domains exhibit distributional shifts, heterogeneous structure, and multi-scale dynamics absent from training data.
approach: SENDAI combines simulation-derived priors with learned discrepancy corrections in a hierarchical framework, reconstructing full spatial states from hyper-sparse observations.
contribution: Achieves 185% maximum SSIM improvement over traditional baselines and 36% improvement over high-frequency methods on satellite vegetation index reconstruction.

problem: Clinical abnormality grounding for rare diseases is hindered by data scarcity, making supervised fine-tuning infeasible and single-pass inference unstable.
approach: Dynamic Decision Learning enables frozen LVLMs to refine decisions through multi-pass visual perturbations and instruction optimization, producing consensus-based reliability scores.
contribution: Improves mAP@75 by up to 105% on rare-disease cases and surpasses adaptation baselines, with stronger calibration under distribution shifts.

problem: Estimating repeatedly nested expectations with quantum computing is expensive classically, but quantum speedups for single nested expectations do not trivially extend to repeated nesting.
approach: Proposes a quantum algorithm achieving epsilon-error with cost ~O(epsilon^-1) via derandomized Multilevel Monte Carlo, overcoming variable-time issues in quantized randomized algorithms.
contribution: Achieves nearly quadratic speedup over classical algorithms, theoretically optimal up to logarithmic factors.

problem: Graph neural networks for SAT tasks model formulas using bipartite graphs or DAGs, missing clause-level and higher-order interactions and failing to capture polarity relationships between literals.
approach: Models SAT formulas as clause-literal hypergraphs with polarity-aware decomposition separating variable representations into invariant and equivariant components.
contribution: Improves unsat-core prediction through explicit modeling of polarity properties and higher-order structural interactions on multiple SAT datasets.

problem: Verifier-free RL for LLM reasoning samples traces independently from answers, decoupling reasoning from answer information and causing inefficient exploration and incoherence.
approach: Coupled Variational Reinforcement Learning (CoVRL) bridges variational inference and RL by coupling prior and posterior distributions through hybrid sampling, enabling efficient exploration with strong thought-answer coherence.
contribution: Improves performance 12.4% over the base model and achieves 2.3% additional improvement over verifier-free RL baselines on mathematical and general reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Large vision-language models achieve strong spatial grounding but have high inference costs, while compact VLMs are efficient but suffer substantial localization degradation under standard training.
approach: DocVAL uses validated chain-of-thought distillation with a rule-based dual-mode validator filtering low-quality signals and providing pixel-level corrective feedback.
contribution: Yields 6-7 ANLS point improvements over comparable compact VLMs with student models that operate without OCR at inference, introducing mAP as a localization metric.

problem: Collaborative machine learning requires incentivizing data sources to share high-quality data, but existing valuation methods do not verify or incentivize truthfulness, enabling manipulation.
approach: Combines semivalues for fairness with a truthful data valuation function using an unknown validation set, proving that sources maximize expected rewards by submitting true data.
contribution: First mechanism provably ensuring collaborative fairness and incentivizing truthfulness at equilibrium for Bayesian models, validated on synthetic and real-world datasets.

problem: Multi-modal dataset distillation requires expensive checkpoint storage and bi-level optimization, limiting scalability and memory efficiency.
approach: Analytic Parameter Matching (APM) theoretically derives analytic parameters of modal projectors to replace inner-loop optimization, aligning teacher and student projectors.
contribution: Achieves up to 65x storage reduction and 9.6x faster distillation while scaling to 1,000 synthetic pairs, with notable generalization in cross-architecture and zero-shot settings.

problem: Federated text-attributed graph learning with LLMs faces high computational overhead from processing long texts, suboptimal one-shot condensation, and black-box interpretability issues.
approach: DANCE performs round-wise, model-in-the-loop condensation refresh using the latest global model and preserves provenance via locally inspectable evidence packs tracing predictions to source spans.
contribution: Improves performance across 8 TAG datasets by combining graph condensation with dynamic LLM-aware refinement and enhanced interpretability through source attribution.

problem: Visual multi-agent systems suffer a counter-intuitive scaling wall where increasing agent turns degrades performance and inflates token costs due to information loss in text-centric communication.
approach: L^2-VMAS enables inter-agent collaboration with dual latent memories that decouple perception and thinking, using entropy-driven proactive triggering for efficient on-demand memory access.
contribution: Breaks the scaling wall with 2.7-5.4% average accuracy improvement while reducing token usage by 21.3-44.8%, demonstrating strong scalability across backbones and structures.

problem: Using pre-trained AI models to automatically label datasets risks incorporating model errors without guarantees on accuracy, making wholesale replacement of manual labeling impractical.
approach: A method for obtaining probably approximately correct labels by validating pre-trained model predictions nonasymptotically with minimal assumptions.
contribution: Enables cost-effective high-quality dataset curation with theoretical guarantees on labeling error, demonstrated on text, image, and protein folding tasks.

problem: Learning multi-task, multi-agent policies for cooperative temporal objectives remains sample-inefficient and requires retraining for each new task.
approach: Automata-Conditioned Cooperative Multi-Agent RL learns task-conditioned decentralized policies, proving optimality and showing value functions can assign tasks optimally at test time.
contribution: Demonstrates emergent task-aware multi-step coordination with sample-efficient learning of task-adaptive, reusable policies for multiple objectives.

problem: RL for instruction following suffers from sparse rewards when the initial model struggles to generate responses satisfying all constraints, yielding indistinguishable signals that impede learning.
approach: Hindsight Instruction Replay replays failed attempts as successes based on satisfied constraints, performing RL on both original and replayed samples as dual-preference learning.
contribution: Achieves promising results on complex instruction following with less computational budget by enabling learning from partial successes.

problem: Prior-data Fitted Networks for amortized causal inference assume a single pre-training works across all interventional regimes, but this assumption has fundamental theoretical limitations.
approach: Proves that a single observational SCM induces exponentially large interventional distribution space (prior uncoverage), proposing target-specific fine-tuning strategies Point-Wise and Meta-Sampling.
contribution: Demonstrates that fine-tuning is necessary to achieve posterior consistency and local generalization properties in causal effect estimation.

problem: Tabular foundation models struggle with weak early-layer value sensitivity and redundant hidden states because scalar tokenization injects value variation through essentially one-dimensional channels.
approach: LimiX-2M uses RBF-feature tokenization to expand scalars into compact localized features and reorders computation as S→N→F blocks aligned with readout, improving effective rank and efficiency.
contribution: A 2M-parameter model outperforms larger TabPFN-v2 and TabICL baselines on tabular benchmarks while reducing training and inference costs.

problem: Cross-task robotic manipulation requires extracting transferable knowledge from seen tasks, but in-context methods provide only low-level action sequences, causing superficial trajectory imitation.
approach: Decomposes demonstrations into interpretable skill-action pairs and recomposes them via compositional reasoning, using visual-semantic retrieval and skill-coverage-aware libraries.
contribution: Enables zero-shot cross-task generalization by learning composable manipulation skills from demonstrations.

problem: Graph contrastive learning relies on positive samples for learning semantic patterns, but message passing trivializes their maximization, preventing effective learning from positives.
approach: SPGCL mitigates trivialization using Dirichlet energy to identify high-energy features for positive learning and low-energy features for reliable positive sampling.
contribution: Restores learning efficacy of positive samples in GCLs by disentangling message passing effects from contrastive learning, with extensive experimental validation.

problem: Long-term fairness algorithms fail to account for selective labels, which are only revealed when positive decisions are made, creating a mismatch between observed and true fairness.
approach: Uses observed data plus a label predictor model to estimate true fairness by decomposing it into observed fairness and prediction bias, deriving sufficient conditions via confidence bounds.
contribution: Proposes a reinforcement learning algorithm for long-term fair decision-making with selective labels, validated on semisynthetic hiring and lending scenarios.

problem: Sampling from unnormalized densities is expensive because evaluating the energy function is costly, requiring efficient sampler learning without access to data.
approach: Flow Sampling builds on diffusion and flow matching, training with denoising diffusion drift conditioned on noise samples, naturally extending to Riemannian manifolds.
contribution: Achieves strong empirical performance on synthetic energy benchmarks, molecular conformer generation, and sphere/hyperbolic distributions with minimal energy evaluations.

problem: Multi-bit watermarking for LLMs suffers from catastrophic false positive rates when using ECC-based extractors, and rejection thresholds collapse detection sensitivity to random guessing.
approach: BREW introduces a two-stage mechanism: blind message estimation via independent block voting followed by window-shifting verification that validates payload against local edits.
contribution: Achieves TPR of 0.965 with FPR of 0.02 under 10% synonym substitution, solving the high-FPR issue as a solvable structural flaw rather than inherent trade-off.

problem: Token-level credit assignment in RL for LLMs treats all tokens equally, failing to distinguish decisive reasoning steps from routine formatting or fluent filler.
approach: FlowTracer traces answer-targeted reasoning on an attention-induced DAG with edge capacities from aggregated attention weights, extracting flow-based token importances.
contribution: Delivers consistent performance gains on reasoning tasks by enabling learning signals to focus on tokens that route information toward correct answers.

problem: Model-based RL approaches combining MPC with learned models typically rely on gradient-free optimization, which is computationally expensive for high-dimensional control.
approach: Dream-MPC generates candidate trajectories from policy rollouts and optimizes each via gradient ascent using a learned world model and uncertainty regularization.
contribution: Significantly improves policy performance on 24 continuous control tasks, outperforming gradient-free MPC and state-of-the-art baselines.

problem: Large-scale time series models exhibit a scaling paradox where larger models do not always achieve better performance due to few-layer dominance and redundant, under-utilized layers.
approach: Automatically identifies and retains only dominant layers while pruning redundant ones, validated across LLM4TS and TSFM architectures.
contribution: Retaining only 21% of parameters achieves up to 12% accuracy improvement and 2.7x inference speedup, with over 95% task improvements on 8 SOTA models.

problem: Visual autoregressive models fix computation per scale and inflate memory at high resolutions, limiting practical deployment despite strong generation quality.
approach: Visual Implicit Autoregressive Modeling embeds an implicit equilibrium layer trained with Jacobian-Free Backpropagation, exposing a per-scale iteration knob for compute control.
contribution: Achieves FID 2.16 on ImageNet 256x256 with 38.4% parameters of VAR, enabling reduction from 19.24GB to 8.53GB peak memory and doubling throughput.

problem: Diffusion model performance is sensitive to score estimation accuracy, but the accumulation of estimation error through the diffusion process is not well understood.
approach: Derives stepwise Wasserstein error bounds in Gaussian-mixture settings and extends to general distributions with curvature analysis at small times.
contribution: Provides sharp Wasserstein estimates for both VP and VE diffusions, clarifying how score errors propagate through reverse-time SDE and probability-flow ODE.

problem: Tabular anomaly detection with LLMs is challenged by heterogeneous features and reliance on limited one-shot supervised fine-tuning, offering weak signal for learning normal data representation.
approach: DiSPaT uses self-play with f-divergence minimization, where a policy generates synthetic pseudo-anomalies and a discriminator learns to distinguish them from normal data.
contribution: Consistently outperforms LLM-based and classical detectors on diverse tabular anomaly detection benchmarks through progressive alignment with true normal data.
